chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Is-haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: There is no angel in the heavens or on earth who does not ask Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for permission to visit the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). A group descends and a group ascends.
ai.seo_question: Do angels visit the grave of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this tradition to underscore the cosmic reverence for Karbala, portraying the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) as a focal point of angelic devotion where every celestial being seeks Allah's permission to visit. This continuous cycle of descent and ascent highlights the site's unique spiritual gravity, affirming its status not merely as a historical tomb but as a living center of divine connection recognized by the entire created order.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Isḥāq ibn ‘Ammār, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say: There is no angel in the heavens or on earth who does not ask Allāh for permission to go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.). (There is always) a crowd descending (to go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.)) and a crowd ascending (back to the heavens).
